subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Safe Start: Personal Movement Readiness and Self-Management
title: Reteach and varied practice: effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device under transfer
focus: effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device
essentialQuestion: How do I get my own body ready to work, and how do I know when to stop?
privacySafeScenario: Design and run a personal warm-up, effort-management, and stop-rule routine, then revise it after using it across several sessions. Evidence is the written or described routine and its revision, not a measured result.
studentTask: Learner works effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device in a full session the learner runs start to finish without prompting, in a space and on a day they did not choose at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner holds effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device in a full session the learner runs start to finish without prompting, in a space and on a day they did not choose, in whatever version their body and setting allow.
The learner names what degraded first and why, rather than reporting only whether it worked.
The learner compares this occasion with the earlier one and says what actually changed.
adaptationChoices: Every element has a seated, supported, low-impact, and reduced-range version. A learner using a mobility aid, working from a chair, or managing a condition designs the same routine around the movements available to them, and that routine is assessed as fully equivalent.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.

Every element has a seated, supported, low-impact, and reduced-range version. A learner using a mobility aid, working from a chair, or managing a condition designs the same routine around the movements available to them, and that routine is assessed as fully equivalent.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where effort scales described by feel, breath, and speech rather than by device shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
